mainTopic: Ledges over a neighbor's courtyard and היזק ראיה; opening windows into a shared courtyard
overview: This עמוד opens with the end of a משנה about a ledge that sticks out from a house over a neighbor's courtyard. A ledge of a טפח can create a חזקה, and the courtyard owner may object to it. A ledge smaller than a טפח creates no חזקה, and nobody can object. רבי מני teaches that a חזקה on a טפח reaches to four, and אביי explains that this means a ledge one טפח wide and four long may later be widened to four. רב הונא and רב יהודה then argue about whether the courtyard owner may object to a ledge under a טפח. The גמרא shows that both agree היזק ראיה is real damage. They argue only about whether the owner of such a small ledge will end up looking into the courtyard. A new משנה then forbids opening windows into a courtyard shared with partners, and the גמרא explains why the משנה chose the shared courtyard as its case. The עמוד ends with a ברייתא in which two חכמים rule opposite ways on such windows, and רב נחמן begins to comment.

steps.title: End of the משנה: ledges of a handbreadth and smaller
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes its ruling. For a ledge of a טפח the courtyard owner can object. For a ledge under a טפח there is no חזקה and no right to object.
steps.simpleTranslation: …and he (the courtyard owner) can protest. If it is less than a handbreadth, he (the house owner) has no חזקה, and he cannot protest.
steps.whatsHappening: We are reading the closing words of the משנה about a ledge sticking out from a wall over a neighbor's courtyard. It gives the rule for a ledge smaller than a טפח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ledge of a טפח is big enough to actually use, so it can create a חזקה, and the neighbor is allowed to object to it. A ledge smaller than a טפח is too small to count. So it gives no חזקה, and the משנה says 'he cannot protest' without telling us who 'he' is. That missing detail is what רב הונא and רב יהודה will argue about later.

keyTerms.meaning: To protest or object, so that the other person cannot claim you agreed
A right a person gains by using something openly over time without being stopped
A handbreadth, roughly 8–10 cm
Less than

phrases.english: and he can protest.
phrases.notes: This is the courtyard owner. He may object to a ledge of a full handbreadth sticking out over his yard.

phrases.english: Less than a handbreadth –
he has no acquired right,
and he cannot protest.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ledge of a טפח allows the courtyard owner to object and can create a חזקה. A ledge under a טפח creates no חזקה and cannot be objected to.

steps.title: Rabbi Mani: a right to a handbreadth is a right to four
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins with a statement of רבי מני, reported in two ways. Whoever gains a חזקה on a טפח gains a חזקה on four.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי אסי said in the name of רבי מני, and some say רבי יעקב said in the name of רבי מני: If he gained a חזקה on a handbreadth, he gained a חזקה on four.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a short, puzzling rule from רבי מני about how far a חזקה on a ledge reaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two versions of who passed the rule on from רבי מני, either רבי אסי or רבי יעקב, but the rule itself is the same. The rule says a חזקה on one טפח becomes a חזקה on four. It does not say four of what, so the wording needs explaining. The גמרא asks about this in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that analyzes the משנה
'And some say it', meaning there is a second version of who said it
He took possession, he gained a חזקה
Four (here, four handbreadths)

phrases.english: Gemara:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי מָנִי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said that Rabbi Mani said,
and some say it this way:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אָמַר רַבִּי מָנִי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ya'akov said that Rabbi Mani said:
If he gained a right to a handbreadth –
he gained a right to four.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי מָנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the משנה's rule that a טפח ledge creates a חזקה and asks how far that חזקה reaches
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חזקה on a טפח reaches to four טפחים.

steps.title: What does Rabbi Mani mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי מני's short rule actually means.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what רבי מני's rule means. This sets up אביי's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'A handbreadth becomes four' could be read several ways. Four in which direction? Four of what? This is a real question about meaning, not an attack on the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: What
Is he saying
'What is he saying?', asking what a statement means

phrases.english: What is he saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what רבי מני's rule means
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly turns from 'a טפח' into 'four'?

steps.title: אביי explains: one handbreadth wide by four long
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains the rule. If the ledge is one טפח wide and four long, the owner gains the right to widen it to four טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: This is what he is saying: If he gained a חזקה on a ledge one handbreadth wide by four long, he gained a חזקה on a width of four.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question by spelling out the size of ledge that רבי מני had in mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'טפח' is the width of the ledge, meaning how far it sticks out. The ledge must also run four טפחים along the wall. A ledge like that is a usable ledge. Once the neighbor lets it stand, the owner may later widen it to four טפחים.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is what he is saying', the start of an explanation
Width (here, how far the ledge sticks out)
Length (here, how far it runs along the wall)
אביי, a leading אמורא of Babylonia

phrases.english: Abaye said: This is what he is saying:
If he gained a right to a width of a handbreadth along a length of four –
he gained a right to a width of four.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by defining the measurements
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A חזקה on a ledge one טפח wide and four long gives the right to widen it to four טפחים.
steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, רבי מני's rule is about a ledge one טפח wide and four long. A חזקה on that ledge lets the owner widen it to four.

steps.title: רב הונא: only the roof owner cannot object
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's 'less than a טפח… cannot protest' again. רב הונא says this means only the roof owner cannot object to the courtyard owner. The courtyard owner can still object to the roof owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Less than a handbreadth: he has no חזקה and cannot protest.' רב הונא said: They taught this only about the roof owner against the courtyard owner. But the courtyard owner against the roof owner can protest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the last line of the משנה, and רב הונא explains who 'cannot protest'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב הונא's reading, the משנה only means that the roof owner cannot complain about what the courtyard owner does, because a tiny ledge gives him no rights. The courtyard owner, though, can still object to the roof owner, even about a ledge under a טפח. So 'cannot protest' works in one direction only.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They only taught…', which narrows the case a rule covers
The roof owner, meaning the owner of the house with the ledge
The courtyard owner, the neighbor below
רב הונא, an early Babylonian אמורא

steps.confusionAlert: 'Roof owner against courtyard owner' means the roof owner is the one protesting against the courtyard owner. The first name is the side doing the objecting.

phrases.english: 'Less than a handbreadth – he has no acquired right,
and he cannot protest.'
Rav Huna said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בַּעַל הַגָּג בְּבַעַל הֶחָצֵר,
phrases.english: They taught this only about the roof owner against the courtyard owner,
phrases.notes: The roof owner can't stop the courtyard owner from doing things that get in the way of his tiny ledge.

phrases.english: but the courtyard owner against the roof owner –
can protest.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בַּעַל הַגָּג בְּבַעַל הֶחָצֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by going back to the last line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under a טפח, the roof owner cannot object to the courtyard owner, but the courtyard owner can object to the roof owner.

steps.title: רב יהודה: neither side can object
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה disagrees. Even the courtyard owner cannot object to the roof owner about a ledge under a טפח.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה said: Even the courtyard owner against the roof owner cannot protest.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives the opposite reading of the משנה, so the two אמוראים now disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב יהודה, 'cannot protest' works both ways. Not even the courtyard owner can object to a ledge smaller than a טפח. The two אמוראים now disagree, and the גמרא will try to find the reason behind their argument.

keyTerms.meaning: Even
רב יהודה, a student of רב and a leading Babylonian אמורא
Cannot

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said:
Even the courtyard owner against the roof owner
cannot protest.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ בַּעַל חָצֵר בְּבַעַל הַגָּג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב הונא's one-way reading
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under a טפח, neither side can object, not even the courtyard owner.

steps.title: Is their argument about harm caused by seeing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב הונא and רב יהודה disagree about whether היזק ראיה counts as real damage.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say they disagree about damage caused by sight? One master holds it is called damage, and the other holds it is not called damage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a reason for the argument between רב הונא and רב יהודה. A 'לימא' suggestion like this sets up the next move and is often tested or turned down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While using even a tiny ledge, the roof owner can look into the neighbor's yard. רב הונא may hold that היזק ראיה is real damage, which is why the courtyard owner can object. רב יהודה may hold it is not damage, so there is nothing to object to. This is only a proposal, not a final ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Shall we say?', a suggestion that is often turned down later
Damage from being seen, losing privacy
They disagree
'One master holds'
'It is called damage', meaning it counts legally as harm

steps.confusionAlert: A 'לימא' is not the conclusion. The גמרא is only trying out this reason, and it may later explain the argument a different way.

phrases.english: Shall we say they disagree about damage caused by sight –
that one master holds: it is called damage,
phrases.notes: This 'master' is רב הונא, who lets the courtyard owner object.

phrases.english: and the other master holds: it is not called damage?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests the underlying reason for the argument between רב הונא and רב יהודה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the argument between רב הונא and רב יהודה really about whether היזק ראיה counts as damage?
steps.whyThisMatters: היזק ראיה is a major topic in בבא בתרא. Whether it counts as damage shapes many laws about privacy between neighbors.

steps.title: Everyone agrees looking is damage, but this ledge is too small to use
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion from step 7. Both אמוראים agree that היזק ראיה is real damage. רב יהודה's reason is that a ledge under a טפח is only good for hanging things, and the roof owner can turn his face away while hanging them.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone agrees that looking into someone's property counts as damage. But here it is different, because the roof owner can say: 'This ledge is too small to use. What is it good for? Only for hanging things on it. I will turn my face away and hang things on it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the idea from step 7 that the argument is about whether looking counts as damage. It gives a different reason for רב יהודה's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides accept that היזק ראיה is damage. רב יהודה holds that a ledge under a טפח is too narrow to stand on. You can only reach over to hang things, and you can do that without looking into the courtyard.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
Damage caused by looking into someone else's private space
Here it is different
Real use, like standing on it
I will turn my face away

steps.confusionAlert: Do not walk away thinking רב יהודה says looking is allowed. He agrees it is damage. He just holds that this tiny ledge does not lead to looking.

phrases.english: No; everyone agrees
that it is called damage;
phrases.notes: "It" means damage from looking, the idea raised in step 7.

phrases.english: but here it is different, because he can say to him:
phrases.notes: The roof owner is talking to the courtyard owner.

phrases.english: For real use, it is not fit;
what is it fit for? For hanging things on it;
I will turn my face away and hang things on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the explanation suggested in step 7
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the argument depends on whether היזק ראיה counts as damage
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Both agree it is damage. The real question is whether a ledge under a טפח leads to looking at all.

steps.title: רב הונא: the roof owner may get scared and look
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא, the other אמורא, holds that the courtyard owner can answer back: sometimes you will get frightened, and then you will end up looking into my courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one, רב הונא, holds that the courtyard owner can say to him: 'Sometimes you will be frightened.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב הונא still lets the courtyard owner object. It answers the roof owner's claim from the step before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה relied on the roof owner turning his face away. רב הונא says you cannot count on that. A person reaching out high up may get scared and look down into the courtyard.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one, meaning the other side of the argument
Sometimes
You get frightened

steps.whatToRemember: Both אמוראים agree that היזק ראיה is damage. They argue only about whether a ledge under a טפח will lead to looking. רב יהודה says the owner can turn away. רב הונא says he may get scared and look.

phrases.english: And the other one holds: he can say to him:
phrases.notes: "The other one" is רב הונא. Here the courtyard owner is talking to the roof owner.

phrases.english: Sometimes you will be frightened.
phrases.notes: He means that when you get scared, you will end up looking into my courtyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רב הונא's side, answering the roof owner's argument from step 8
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יהודה's argument from step 8: the roof owner can turn his face away while hanging things, so a ledge under a טפח never leads to looking.
steps.terutzMaskana: He may get frightened and look, so the courtyard owner can still object.

steps.title: New משנה: no windows into a shared courtyard
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that a person may not open his windows into a courtyard he shares with partners. The same applies to a house he bought in another courtyard and to a loft he built on his house. Instead, he may build a room inside his house, or a loft that opens into his own house.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person may not open his windows into a courtyard of partners. If he bought a house in a different courtyard, he may not open it into the partners' courtyard. If he built a loft on top of his house, he may not open it into the partners' courtyard. Rather, if he wants, he may build a room inside his house, or build a loft on top of his house and open it into his house.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new rule. You may not make new openings into a courtyard you share with others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives three cases: windows, a house in another courtyard, and a loft. In all three he may not open into the shared courtyard. It ends by showing the allowed way to add space: the new room must open into his own house, not into the courtyard.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
A courtyard owned together by partners
Windows
An upper room or loft
Inside his house

phrases.english: משנה:
A person may not open his windows
into a courtyard of partners.
phrases.notes: This is a courtyard he himself shares with other people.

phrases.english: If he bought a house in a different courtyard,
he may not open it into the partners' courtyard.
If he built a loft on top of his house,
he may not open it into the partners' courtyard;
rather, if he wants,
he may build a room inside his house,
or build a loft on top of his house,
and open it into his house.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ לֹא יִפְתַּח אָדָם חַלּוֹנוֹתָיו לַחֲצַר הַשּׁוּתָּפִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not open windows, a house, or a loft into a shared courtyard. A new room must open into one's own house.

steps.title: Why does the משנה mention only a shared courtyard?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה says only 'a courtyard of partners.' Even into a neighbor's courtyard, a person may not open a window.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does the משנה specifically say 'into a courtyard of partners'? Even into his neighbor's courtyard he may not open a window!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the משנה. Why pick the shared courtyard, when the rule should obviously apply to a neighbor's courtyard too?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a window into a shared courtyard is not allowed, a window into a courtyard that belongs only to someone else should be even more clearly forbidden. So the גמרא wants to know what the משנה adds by choosing the partners' case.

keyTerms.meaning: Why specifically this case?
His neighbor's courtyard
Also

phrases.english: גמרא:
Why specifically into a courtyard of partners?
Even into his neighbor's courtyard he may also not!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the משנה in step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's choice to mention only a courtyard of partners
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule against opening windows should apply even more to a neighbor's courtyard, so mentioning only partners seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The משנה teaches the bigger חידוש: even a shared courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה uses a 'it is not necessary to say' style. A neighbor's courtyard is obviously forbidden. The new point is that even a shared courtyard is forbidden, because a window takes away privacy the partner still had inside his house.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is saying 'it goes without saying.' It goes without saying that you may not open a window into your neighbor's courtyard. But you might have thought a shared courtyard is different, because the window owner can say: 'In the end, you already have to keep yourself private from me in the courtyard.' So the משנה teaches that the partner can answer: 'Until now I only had to be private from you in the courtyard. Now I would have to be private from you even inside my house.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 11. The משנה mentions a shared courtyard because that is the case with the new teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a shared courtyard, you might think a window adds no new harm, since the partners already see each other there. The משנה rejects this. A window lets the owner see into the partner's house, and the house was private until now. That is new היזק ראיה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is not necessary to say.' The easy case is obvious, and the text teaches the harder case.
A courtyard owned together by partners
To keep oneself private and hidden from view
'It teaches us.' This introduces the new point being taught.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think a shared courtyard is more forbidden than a neighbor's courtyard. It is the opposite. A shared courtyard is the case where you might have allowed the window, so the משנה mentions it to teach that even there it is forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule that even partners, who already see each other in the courtyard, can block a new window that looks into their home.

phrases.english: It is saying 'it is not necessary':
It is not necessary to say that into his neighbor's courtyard he may not,
but into a courtyard of partners,
where he can say to him: 'In the end,'
phrases.notes: The 'he' here is the man who wants to open the window. He is arguing with his partner.

phrases.aramaic: הָא קָא בָּעֵית אִצְטְנוֹעֵי מִינַּאי בֶּחָצֵר;
phrases.english: 'you already need to keep private from me in the courtyard.'
It teaches us that he can say to him:
'Until now, in the courtyard'
'I needed to keep private from you.'
'Now, even in the house'
'I also need to keep private from you.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 11 about why the משנה said 'shared courtyard'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: לא מיבעיא: the משנה teaches the less obvious case, and the more obvious case is understood on its own.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Into a shared courtyard you might have been allowed to open a window, since the partners already have to stay private from each other there.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even into a shared courtyard it is forbidden, because the window takes away privacy inside the house.

steps.title: A story: two sages rule differently about windows into a shared courtyard
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells of a man who opened windows into a shared courtyard. רבי ישמעאל בר רבי יוסי told him he had gained a right to keep them. רבי חייא told him to close them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: A man once opened his windows into a shared courtyard. He came before רבי ישמעאל בר רבי יוסי, who told him: 'You have gained the right, my son, you have gained the right.' He came before רבי חייא, who said: 'You worked hard to open them. Now work hard and close them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a real case about our משנה's rule. Two חכמים gave opposite rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל בר רבי יוסי held that the man had gained a חזקה, a right to keep the windows, so the partners could no longer stop him. רבי חייא held that he had no such right and had to seal the windows, which fits our משנה. The story itself does not explain why they disagree. רב נחמן's comment, which begins in the next step and continues on the next עמוד, takes this up.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The רבנן taught.' This opens a ברייתא.
'You have gained a חזקה.' This means you have gained a right to keep it that way.
'You worked hard' or 'you toiled'
'Seal it' or 'close it up'

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
There was an incident with one man
who opened his windows into a courtyard of partners;

phrases.aramaic: וּבָא לִפְנֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בַּר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי,
phrases.english: and he came before Rabbi Yishmael bar Rabbi Yosei,
who said to him: 'You have gained the right, my son, you have gained the right.'
And he came before Rabbi Chiya,
who said: 'You worked hard and opened them,'
'now work hard and seal them.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּאָדָם אֶחָד שֶׁפָּתַח חַלּוֹנָיו לַחֲצַר הַשּׁוּתָּפִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real case about the משנה's rule on windows into a shared courtyard.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי ישמעאל בר רבי יוסי ruled that the window owner had gained a חזקה and could keep the windows. רבי חייא ruled that he must seal them.

steps.title: רב נחמן begins to comment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces רב נחמן, who is about to comment, most likely on the story just told. His words come on the next עמוד.
steps.whatsHappening: This is only an opening line. The גמרא is setting up רב נחמן's statement, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing has been said yet. Coming right after the story of the two opposite rulings, רב נחמן will probably explain or settle the disagreement between רבי ישמעאל בר רבי יוסי and רבי חייא.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא whose statement is about to be given

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens an אמורא's statement that will follow the ברייתא story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not yet stated. Only the attribution to רב נחמן appears here.
